newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels' military chief reported killed.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels' military chief reported killed.

text.p: The military commander of the rebels in eastern Zaire has been killed in an ambush, probably by Mai-Mai tribal warriors, security sources said on Monday.
After days of rumours in rebel-held areas about Andre Kisase Ngandu, the sources said he was killed on or about January 8 near the rebel-held town of Butembo.
There was no official confirmation from Laurent Kabila, chairman of the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL).

Ngandu was a prominent figure in the Rwandan-backed Alliance that routed Zairean government troops in a rapid offensive starting last October. It now controls a strip of territory more than 600 km (400 miles) long against Zaire's eastern border with Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi.
"His death has been a big blow for the rebels but they are getting by," one security source in the region told Reuters in Nairobi by telephone, declining to be quoted by name.
Rebel areas are steeled for a promised counter-offensive by Zaire's army, reported to be reorganising in Kisangani and Kindu with the help of foreign mercenaries.
One security source said Ngandu was killed when his military convoy was ambushed by Mai-Mai fighters outside Butembo, 180 km (110 miles) north of the rebel capital Goma.
The Mai-Mai of North Kivu province are drawn from indigenous tribes who believe their magic makes them invulnerable.

Tactical partners of the Alliance forces during the early weeks of the rebellion, many Mai-Mai are now opposed to rebels they consider dominated by ethnic Tutsis close to the Rwandan army and government.
Kabila and the Alliance threatened a crackdown against some Mai-Mai leaders after rebel troops were attacked in the first week of January.
One foreign resident in Goma, the rebel capital, said the town had been rife with rumours about Ngandu for several days.
"There are rumours about an internal struggle in the Alliance and others that Ngandu was killed or badly injured," the resident said.
Like Kabila, Ngandu was a veteran foe of Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko who seized power in 1965. Mobutu is ailing with cancer and returned for treatment in Europe this month.
Despite the dominance of Banyamulenge Tutsis in the Alliance forces, Kabila is from North Shaba province and Ngandu from the diamond-rich Kasai.
Ngandu was chairman of the National Resistance Council for Democracy (CNRD), one of the Alliance's key components.

A statement faxed to Nairobi on Monday and purporting to come from the CNRD said Major-General Ngandu and his aides were assassinated by "armed elements in the service of Kabila" near Butembo on January 8.
The statement, dated Goma on Monday but apparently sent from neighbouring Uganda, was signed anonymously by "J.B. of General Ngandu's protocol service".

The rebels have not reported any further gains in the past fortnight against Mobutu's troops. Diplomatic sources say they are recruiting heavily with new troops deployed in safe areas while more experienced rebels guard the western front-line against a government counter-attack.
